channel.title: Business Administration A · Study Podcast
channel.description: Two-host study episodes for Business Administration A (HSG, Autumn 2026): lectures, readings, models and exam practice.
channel.itunes:author: Adrián

item.title: Episode 6 · Innovation I · Lego, Ambidexterity and Growth
item.description: Lecture 5 of Business Administration A, explained step by step. VRIO and absorptive capacity, the Lego story from crisis to comeback, exploitation versus exploration, the three types of ambidexterity, multidexterity, the Ansoff matrix with examples, related versus unrelated diversification, open innovation with Lego Ideas, and business model innovation. Quiz questions have pauses so you can answer.

item.title: Episode 5 · Strategy II · Resources and Capabilities
item.description: Lecture 4 of Business Administration A, explained step by step. Why profits differ inside one industry, the market-based versus resource-based view, tangible and intangible resources, Porter's value chain, VRIN and the step-by-step competitive analysis, explicit and tacit knowledge, dynamic capabilities (sensing, seizing, reconfiguring), absorptive capacity, the four SWOT questions, and how much industry versus firm explains performance. Quiz questions have pauses so you can answer.

item.title: Episode 4 · Strategy I · Porter's Five Forces
item.description: Lecture 3 of Business Administration A, explained step by step. What strategy is and isn't, Rumelt's core of good strategy, Porter's five forces one by one with the conditions and examples, the ASML case, PESTEL, M&A and the Bayer case, economic moats, why firms and regulators want opposite things, plus Porter's generic strategies and the three management levels from the course book. Quiz questions have pauses so you can answer.

item.title: Episode 3 · Alliances, Networks and Platforms
item.description: Lecture 2 of Business Administration A, explained step by step. Hybrid governance between market and hierarchy, the five types of interorganizational relationships, what holds alliances together (contracts, trust, relational norms), termination rights, networks, and how digital platforms create value through match making, market making, trust building and network effects, with the formulas worked through. Quiz questions have pauses so you can answer.

item.title: Episode 2 · Why Do Firms Exist?
item.description: Lecture 1 (part 2) of Business Administration A, explained step by step. The economic problem, division of labour from Adam Smith to the F1 pit stop, Taylor and business as a science, transaction costs and make-or-buy (Coase), vertical integration at Tesla, asset specificity, uncertainty and frequency, the hold-up problem worked through as a game, and the five theories of the firm. Quiz questions have pauses so you can answer.

item.title: Episode 1 · Value Creation and the St. Gallen Management Model
item.description: Lecture 1 (part 1) and Reading W1 of Business Administration A, explained step by step. How the course and exam work, what "value" really means, the St. Gallen Management Model layer by layer, and the three tools from the reading (locating a challenge, the causal chain, and from stakeholder to consequence), each with a worked example. Quiz questions have pauses so you can answer.
